questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Any destination was crucial to me, since I really did not want to to my BSc in a gruop, and by studying abroad I could write it up solo.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved studying abroad, the only thing that did not go according to plan was the distrubution of Erasmus+ scholarship... my home university, University of Copenhagen, did not want to distribute the scholarship until march because of some 'technical issues' with my 'irish tax number', which does not exist since I did not go to Ireland to work, but to study. This only happened to me and none of my friends.... Anyway, I had to fight with UCPHabroad to get them to distribute my Scholarship, and this took a lot of my energy.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The people at my host institution were very helpful. Sadly, I could not attend the orientation week due to exams at my home university - but everyone was welcoming and tried their best to keep me up to date.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different accomodations to variable prices - I lived in the cheapest accommodation on campus, which was very expensive.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We did not have an oven in our appartment on campus - we could use the communal oven, but it was very unsanitary and dirty.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive, but it was all worth it in the end, because you get to know so many people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No oven, mini fridge for four people - not enough space.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The host institution sent out a date, were we could register and apply for on-campus accommodation.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could contact the people in charge if we needed help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful. I got all my top-three modules.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Carefully read all the emails, the host institution sends out - all the information is there. Be quick to register/apply for in campus accommodation, as it is popular and there are not enough rooms for everone.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very nice, very different from my home university.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did my BSc thesis worth 15 ECTS +  three courses, worth 5 ECTS each = 30 ECTS in total

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: it was easier, but then again I have not tried electives courses back home, so I dont know how these compare as they are often 'easier'.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Leading teams in the scientific enterprise
Drug action II
Hot Topics
BSc project

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Leading teams in the scientific enterprise - no exam, gives you more time to focus and work on your thesis and meet knew people.
Drug action II - This course resembles 'Organfarmakologi' and ' Systemfarmakologi'
Hot Topics - no exam, gives you more time to work on your Thesis...

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Im not sure. We went on 'spontaneous' trips and hikes, but I expected this.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Definitly food in supermarkets. E.g. 1kg of greek yoghurt was 1.69 euros, 12 DKK, whereas 1kg in Denmark is 32 DKK
Alcohol was the same and so was dining out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UCD has so many clubs and societies. I joined the Canoe club

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Endless activities. UCD is a big campus and they do a lot of activities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Res-Life.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You should totally visit Dun Laoghaire, Bray, Belfast, Galway, Cliffs of Moher.... the list goes on

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, th Irish are super helpful

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I dont, I wish i socialized more with local students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the way they work in Ireland is more 'layed back' and not that structured, at least where I worked...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The irish people<3 and the beautiful nature

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy, it is going to be amazing. Choose easy courses to you will have more free time

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: bring a rain coat/wind breaker, it literally rains every day and it is very windy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met. They are wonderful

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Doing my exam in the RDS exam hall. Over 1000 students take their exam in the same hall. It was giving Hunger Games vibes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
